妥.meaning: A <part>woman</part> runs the claw machine at the fair, and children keep crying when the metal <part>claw</part> drops their prizes. So she oils it, tunes it and slows it right down, until it lowers each teddy into a child's arms as softly as a kiss. Now it's the most <kanji>gentle</kanji> machine at the fair.
妥.on: Its favourite prize is a yellow rubber <sound>du</sound>ck, which it sets down on the counter without a squeak.

盆.meaning: A potter drops her best flat <part>dish</part> and it breaks into a dozen pieces. She glues each <part>part</part> back with its edge tilted up, so it comes out deeper than before. Rain fills it overnight, and by morning two sparrows are splashing in her new <kanji>basin</kanji>.
盆.on: She dries the shivering sparrows beside a crackling <sound>bon</sound>fire in the yard.

騰.meaning: At a midnight rodeo, a <part>flailing man</part> clings to a bucking <part>horse</part>. With every kick the horse springs higher, until the rider's hat bumps the <part>moon</part> and the crowd gasps. Prices at the hot-dog stand do the same thing all night: <kanji>leaping up</kanji>.
騰.on: When they finally land, the horse stamps on the rider's big <sound>toe</sound>, and he hops round the ring.
騰.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' yells the rider, waving a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic to calm the horse before the next jump.

胞.meaning: Before a baby is born, it gets a packed lunch every day: a soft round cushion, pale as the <part>moon</part>, where the mother can <part>pack up</part> food and air and send them down a cord. Nine months of deliveries. When the baby arrives, the empty lunchbox follows: the <kanji>placenta</kanji>.
胞.on: The new dad is so excited he waters the whole street with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.

卑.meaning: The palace's newest servant gets the lowest job of all: weeding the king's <part>rice field</part> <part>ten</part> times a day, bent double, while a <part>slash</part> of muddy rain runs down his back. Even the king's goat outranks him. No job in the land is more <kanji>lowly</kanji>.
卑.on: The goat even nibbles the <sound>hee</sound>l of his boot while he works.
卑.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' he squeals, as the goat runs off with his ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn.

涙.meaning: A clown's job is to make children laugh, but every autumn, when the circus has to <part>return</part> to its winter barn, <part>water drops</part> squirt from the flower on his jacket and run down his painted cheeks. The children think it's a trick. It isn't. Those are real <kanji>tears</kanji>.
涙.on: The barn is nearly an old <sound>rui</sound>n, with a hole where the roof should be.
涙.kun: He shares warm <sound>na</sound>an with a <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a <sound>du</sound>ck, who sniffle along with him.

盾.meaning: A nervous goalkeeper practises at the foot of a <part>cliff</part>. Rocks bounce down; he counts to <part>ten</part>, peeks out with one <part>eye</part> from behind an old saucepan lid, and every rock clangs off it. He has never saved a ball, but he's found the perfect <kanji>shield</kanji>.
盾.on: Between rockfalls, he leans the lid against a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush to rest his arm.
盾.kun: He hides under it to eat a <sound>ta</sound>co in his little <sound>te</sound>nt.

械.meaning: A bossy park ranger bolts a gadget into an old <part>tree</part>: cogs, pulleys and a loudspeaker that barks each park <part>commandment</part> at passers-by. No picnics, no ball games, no fun. Then a squirrel jams an acorn in the gears and it squeaks to a halt. So much for his <kanji>contraption</kanji>.
械.on: Before it broke, its grabbing arm caught a child's <sound>ki</sound>te and wouldn't let go.
械.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp from the pond flops up and <sound>se</sound>ts the kite free.

鉛.meaning: A clumsy alchemist tries to turn grey slop into <part>gold</part> by pouring it through a magic <part>funnel</part>. He gets it backwards: his gold ring slips in, and out drips something dull, soft and so heavy it falls through the floor. He has invented <kanji>lead</kanji>.
鉛.on: It lands with a clunk on the <sound>en</sound>gine of the car in his cellar.
鉛.kun: His neighbour uses the flat lump to press <sound>na</sound>an for her <sound>ma</sound>ma and to sink a fishing line by the <sound>ree</sound>f.

厄.meaning: A grumpy postman lives in a hut under a <part>cliff</part>. Every letter that crosses his desk gets a big red <part>stamp</part> of a broken mirror. Whoever opens one trips on the stairs, loses a sock and gets rained on. Nobody in town wants to be that <kanji>unlucky</kanji>.
厄.on: He keeps one spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca on his counter, and it pricks everyone who reaches for their mail.

粋.meaning: A tiny café at a crossroads has no shop sign, just a wooden <part>signpost</part> wearing a silk scarf and sunglasses, one arm pointing at a bowl of plain <part>rice</part> on the doorstep. Fashion models queue round the block. Plain rice has never looked so <kanji>chic</kanji>.
粋.on: Each bowl comes with one wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t balanced on top.
粋.kun: The doorman is an <sound>ee</sound>l in a bow tie, with a gold <sound>key</sound> round his neck.

翼.meaning: An inventor glues <part>feathers</part> to two old doors, a <part>different</part> kind on each: pigeon on the left, peacock on the right. He leaps off the barn and flies in circles all afternoon, fast and very lopsided. Next time he'll match each <kanji>wing</kanji>.
翼.on: He lands face first in a frying pan, with egg <sound>yo</sound>lk on his nose.
翼.kun: He sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', blowing feathers across the <sound>ba</sound>rn and into a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

稚.meaning: A young <part>sparrow</part> is put in charge of guarding the farm's <part>grain</part> from the other birds. Instead he eats it, throws it at the hens and sulks when the scarecrow won't play tag with him. The farmer sighs. Still far too <kanji>immature</kanji> for the job.
稚.on: Next he dares a <sound>chee</sound>tah at the zoo to a race, and loses before he flaps once.
稚.kun: He cheeps '<sound>Ee</sound>!' at a <sound>to</sound>rch, pecks a <sound>ke</sound>ttle, steals the farmer's <sound>na</sound>an and cheeps '<sound>Ee</sound>!' again.

拾.meaning: A tidy sailor never drops his <part>anchor</part> for nothing. Each time he hauls it up, something is hooked on it: a boot, a bottle, a teapot lid that's a perfect <part>fit</part> for his own teapot. The bay is spotless now. He sails around just to <kanji>pick up</kanji> litter.
拾.on: Today the anchor brings up one giant <sound>shoe</sound>, full of crabs.
拾.kun: The shoe has a broken <sound>hee</sound>l and a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket stuck in its toe.

胎.meaning: A tiny astronaut floats in a warm round capsule with no windows, tethered by a cord. Each night his mum rests her bump on a pillow like a <part>pedestal</part> and sings to him under the <part>moon</part>. In nine months he'll land. For now, his spaceship is the <kanji>womb</kanji>.
胎.on: His dad is already practising his smartest <sound>tie</sound> knot for the big day.

宙.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part> of his workshop, a professor pins up a note with the <part>reason</part> things fall: gravity. A balloon knocks out the pin and the note drifts away. Now the teapot, the cat and the professor all bob below the ceiling. Without the reason, everything hangs in <kanji>mid-air</kanji>.
宙.on: The professor blows a bubble of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum and steers himself to the door with it.

維.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> perches on a sleeping farmer's ankle, tugs a loose <part>thread</part> from his sock and flies off with it. The sock gets shorter and shorter; by noon he's barefoot and her nest is woolly. Under a magnifying glass, each strand is a thousand hairs: <kanji>fiber</kanji> after fiber.
維.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l in the pond asks to borrow some to knit a scarf.

繊.meaning: A tightrope walker stretches one <part>thread</part> from a <part>spear</part> stuck in the <part>soil</part> to a stand of <part>candles</part> on the town hall roof. She tiptoes across so lightly the flames don't flicker. The crowd gasps: she and her thread are both so <kanji>slender</kanji>.
繊.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try below holds out a net, just in case.

宇.meaning: A wizard's cottage has a <part>roof</part> so wide its edges stick out far past the walls. Visitors hang their pointy hats on the <part>hat stand</part> by his door and stay dry while it pours, and pigeons nest all along the overhang. The best seat in the rain is under the <kanji>eaves</kanji>.
宇.on: There the wizard slurps a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don while the rain drums above.

喪.meaning: Since the old dog died, the boy wears his grandad's black <part>garment</part> every day. <part>Ten</part> times a day his <part>mouth</part> opens to whistle for her, and then he remembers. The house is quiet, and nobody tells him to stop. It's normal to <kanji>miss</kanji> someone.
喪.on: He keeps her collar beside the <sound>soa</sound>p in the bathroom, where he sees it every morning.
喪.kun: At dusk a grey <sound>mo</sound>th settles on his black sleeve and stays very still.

紫.meaning: A weaver dyes her wool with beetroot and blueberries and hangs each wet skein of <part>thread</part> on the kitchen <part>spoon rack</part> to dry. The colours drip into each other, red into blue, and by morning every strand and every spoon is the same royal shade: <kanji>purple</kanji>.
紫.on: A knight buys the lot to paint his <sound>shi</sound>eld.
紫.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se cheers, '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and wraps one strand round a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin and a <sound>key</sound>.

胆.meaning: A night watchman who's scared of the dark finally walks his whole round under the <part>moon</part> without hiding once. At <part>daybreak</part> the doctor finds his secret: a little green bag under his liver, full of bitter juice and swollen with pride. His courage lives in his <kanji>gall bladder</kanji>.
胆.on: Last night he even walked through the old railway <sound>tun</sound>nel.
胆.kun: At the far end he found a rusty <sound>key</sound> and a sleepy <sound>mo</sound>th.

懇.meaning: A shy <part>robot</part> wants friends, so it bolts a big red <part>heart</part> to its chest and clanks into the jungle. A <part>leopard</part> sniffs it, purrs and takes it to the waterhole, where it shakes every paw and pours the tea. It's the most <kanji>sociable</kanji> robot ever built.
懇.on: Even a grumpy <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down for a cup.
懇.kun: <sound>Ne</sound>xt, they all play bi<sound>ngo</sound>, and the robot calls out the numbers.

阻.meaning: A general plants his <part>pennant</part> on a hill to claim it. His rival stacks a crate in front of it, and <part>moreover</part> another on top, and another, until the flag is hidden behind a wall of boxes and nobody can find the hill. Every plan the general makes, the rival manages to <kanji>thwart</kanji>.
阻.on: Then he drags a squashy <sound>so</sound>fa across the only path up.
阻.kun: The general plays a sad tune on his <sound>ha</sound>rp in the <sound>ba</sound>rn.

狙.meaning: A fisherman climbs onto a crate, and <part>moreover</part> a second crate on top, to get a better angle. He squints for an hour, then swings his line: the <part>fishhook</part> sails past three seagulls and snags the lake's only sunken treasure chest. Patience is everything when you <kanji>aim at</kanji> something.
狙.on: His wife watches from a <sound>so</sound>fa she has dragged down to the shore.
狙.kun: He scoops the chest into his <sound>ne</sound>t, and the seagulls cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

挟.meaning: At the harbour, a sailor drops his <part>anchor</part> and his two little nephews run up for a <part>group hug</part>. He squeezes so hard that the boy in the middle squeaks, wedged between his uncle's arms like a sandwich filling. It's meant as a hug, but it feels like a <kanji>pinch</kanji>.
挟.on: '<sound>Kyo</sound>to,' he says, stretching out the start, when they ask where he's sailing next.
挟.kun: The nephews give him a <sound>ha</sound>rp and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines for the trip.

汗.meaning: In a heatwave, an old wooden <part>drying rack</part> holds up fourteen wet towels, three duvets and a cat. It creaks, it groans, and <part>water drops</part> bead all over its poles. By evening the laundry is dry, but the rack isn't: it's dripping with <kanji>sweat</kanji>.
汗.on: The family pins a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to it for being so brave.
汗.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' it creaks, as the sun <sound>se</sound>ts at last.

賀.meaning: Every time a pearl diver comes up with a <part>shellfish</part>, her crew <part>add</part> it to the pile and cheer louder. By the hundredth they're dancing, singing and hugging the seagulls, and the last shell holds a pearl the size of a plum. The whole boat is pure <kanji>joy</kanji>.
賀.on: That night they party on deck with prawns and <sound>ga</sound>rlic bread.

渉.meaning: A postman's van breaks down at a river, so he takes off his boots and goes for a <part>walk</part> straight through the cold <part>water drops</part>, mailbag on his head and fish nibbling his toes. Every letter arrives on time. No bridge needed: he knows where to <kanji>ford</kanji> it.
渉.on: On the far bank the villagers clap as if it's a <sound>show</sound>.
渉.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' he yells as a fish nips him, and drops his <sound>ta</sound>co in the river.

拭.meaning: At a ship's naming <part>ceremony</part>, the mayor swings the bottle, misses the hull and soaks the admiral. Then the crew hauls up the muddy <part>anchor</part> and it drips all over the band. A cabin boy runs along the deck with one tiny towel. He has a lot to <kanji>wipe</kanji>.
拭.on: When he dries the band's microphone, he gets a little <sound>shock</sound>.
拭.kun: Afterwards he hides in a <sound>noo</sound>k below deck with a <sound>goo</sound>die bag of sweets.
